newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL expects improved second half.
newsitem.headline: INL expects improved second half.

text.p: New Zealand's Independent Newspapers Ltd said on Monday it expected an improved result in the second half-year over the previous corresponding period.

"A slight lift in advertising revenues has occurred early in the second half which, together with the impact of newsprint reductions, should enable the company to produce improved trading results over the same period last year," the company said in a statement. INL added: "However, further restructuring costs at Gordon and Gotch Australia and some additional write offs in relation to Terramedia will be brought to charge in this period."
INL earlier reported a net profit of NZ$26.19 million in the six months to December 31, up from $25.96 million in the previous corresponding period.
Net profit in the year to June 30, 1996 was NZ$47.18 million.
Gordon and Gotch is a magazine distributor, and Teramedia is a CD rom publishing business in the United States.

INL said its half-year trading result before tax and unusual items was up 10.7 percent at NZ$48.8 million, a "satisfactory" outcome in view of difficult trading conditions in its major areas of operation in both New Zealand and Australia.
Revenues at $475.7 million were flat, with depressed retail advertising volumes in both New Zealand and Australia and a further contraction in Australian magazine distribution activities.

INL said its New Zealand papers turned in especially pleasing results. Tight control of costs, some growth in national advertising volumes and steady circulation figures were translated into improved operating margins.
It said strong growth in its New Zealand magazine distribution division continued through the six months.
The restructuring of Gordon and Gotch in Australia accounted for the greater part of the $2.4 million severance payments made in the six months, up from $2.1 million for the same period last year.

The other major item in non-trading expenses for the period was a provision of $1.3 million in respect of development costs write downs by the Teramedia following disappointing sales of the award-winning CD roms Space Station Alpha and Dinamation Adventure.

Terabyte in New Zealand registered an improved performance for the period, securing major new contracts with Auckland International Airport, the Museum of New Zealand and web sites for major corporates.
In the United States, Houston Community Newspapers again performed well and significantly ahead of last year, and West Coast Community Newspapers registered a slightly improved performance, INL said.
Debt, net of deposits of $69.6 million, was lowered during the period and stood at $38.5 million at December 31, compared to $65.7 million at June 30, 1996.
